mfrmr roadmap

Source: ROADMAP.md

Updated 2026-10-26. mfrmr 0.2.4 is a release candidate and has not been released. Its purpose is to connect rating-based measurement, assessment planning and useful feedback. The immediate priority is to finish these workflows with their meanings intact, then qualify and publish the matching package and documentation.

User question Available in the candidate Remaining boundary or next work
What can be measured after accounting for the rating process? RSM/PCM and bounded GPCM workflows; estimates, diagnostics, target-specific uncertainty, figures and saved scoring. Two-family GPCM and common-plan inference retain their experimental scope. Numerical delivery is not a coverage guarantee.
How many ratings are needed for the intended score? Supported G/D studies, fixed score components/composites, plan comparisons, uncertainty and reports. Future plans are complete balanced projections; arbitrary sparse future rosters and automatic cost-optimal allocation are not implemented.
What should raters or assessment developers review? Severity, fit, agreement, specified bias screens, anchor/link reviews, model-choice reports and individual feedback. Screens are not fairness verdicts. Anchor readiness is not invariance; the review cannot supply missing drift evidence.
Can the analysis be reported and reused faithfully? Shared report/appendix routes, long plot tables, editable measurement/G/D/review templates and user-declared study context. Explain data transformations and score direction across analyses. Shared metadata does not make raw G-study scores equivalent to latent measures.
What must happen before release? A matching local candidate, scoped numerical/workflow evidence, distributed regression and attributed repairs. Integrate the selected source, finish remaining platform/external-link/website checks and verify authorized publication. Source identification remains separate from release qualification.

Recent network extensions are one part of feedback, not the organizing goal of the package. Design graphs, signed agreement, SWS/PUS, halo contrasts and binary ERGMs answer different questions and retain their documented limitations.

After 0.2.4, prioritize reusable inference and score/event specifications, then bounded multidimensional rubric measurement. Response/production time and rater scoring time remain distinct observations; continuous-dimension Q matrices and discrete-attribute Q matrices remain distinct specifications. Bayesian fitting, latent classes and cognitive diagnosis are staged research and implementation plans, not capabilities established by their inclusion here. See staged delivery.

The detailed scope below records method-specific conditions. Start with the workflow requirements, three pillars, or release milestones. Use NEWS for changes and migration and README for a first analysis.

Focus for 0.2.4

The release has three complementary purposes:

Purpose Question it helps answer Current priority
Measurement models How do ability, rater severity, category use and discrimination explain ratings? Make the implemented models, diagnostics and uncertainty estimates usable with explicit limits.
G-theory assessment planning How would tasks, raters and score weights affect assessment dependability? Preserve the completed, scoped estimates, intervals and plan comparisons in the final API and release.
Rater feedback and assessment decisions Which rating patterns need review, and how uncertain is a conclusion? Connect supported diagnostics, individual reports and decision summaries.

The G-theory interval requirements are reconciled within the documented designs and assumptions, with experimental methods distinguished from qualified defaults. Anchor alignment and its migration workflow are checked within the supported scope. Final package and environment verification follows the required feature work. Measurement and feedback remain part of 0.2.4, with unfinished research distinguished from implemented features. The earlier numerical and help corrections remain accepted within their scope. The final API decisions now include consistent validation of the reviewed saved-result consumers and settled primary-entry and naming conventions. The candidate includes breaking API changes. The compatibility guide maps replaced calls, arguments and result structures to the supported interfaces and explains effects on saved-result reuse. The review of mathematical validity, numerical accuracy, stability and algorithmic efficiency now supports the documented claims and restrictions. Experimental methods have a checked calculation basis while retaining their unresolved inference limitations; the label alone is not their justification. Check, CI and documentation-build execution-time requirements follow substantive specification freeze. See the completion milestones for their dependencies and acceptance conditions. The package is intended for different assessment settings whose rating designs match the selected method’s assumptions.

FACETS and GENOVA compatibility: release scope and follow-up

The implemented compatibility options below belong to 0.2.4 within their checked scope. Unchecked investigations remain unfinished and are identified as follow-up work; they are not claims of software equivalence. Their release allocation rests on the independent calculation checks and explicit model restrictions below. A wrong calculation within the supported scope, an unimplemented promised option or a misleading comparison remains a release blocker. Documenting a difference does not complete its numerical explanation.

Compatibility is assessed per quantity. Independently derived model calculations remain the statistical basis; verified ordinary-JML reporting conventions can match FACETS to support migration and comparison. Unexplained version-specific outputs are not reproduced by empirical corrections. Compatibility options must retain the estimand, primary estimates and inference qualifications; they do not imply that FACETS defines G-theory or all supported estimation methods.

Intended uses and evidence

mfrmr aims to help users explain ratings, plan assessments and communicate the uncertainty of their conclusions. The same three purposes serve practical assessment and research on theoretical constructs. Language assessment is the main teaching context; configurable facet roles and score definitions support other applications without requiring separate domain-specific analysis APIs.

Setting A question worth answering Relevant evidence and limits
Language assessment and speech contests Would more tasks or raters improve a specified score, and which rubric or rating patterns need review? G/D-study components and plan comparisons, MFRM category/fit diagnostics and supported feedback. Define whether the target is performance on this speech or proficiency across tasks. Annual comparisons require the separate common-recording workflow.
Music performance assessment How much do pieces, judges and their interactions affect scores for technique or expression? Map performers, judges, pieces and fixed score components to the supported design. State whether pieces are sampled or fixed. An example of the mapping is not empirical validation in music.
Judged sports How sensitive is a judged performance score to judges, routines and rubric weights? Use the observed-score or ordered-category route appropriate to the scoring rules. Reliability and severity estimates do not provide winner probabilities, and these models do not automatically apply to race times or match outcomes.
Construct-focused research Are rubric categories, criterion relations and task/rater dependencies consistent with a stated interpretation of the score? Category, fit, residual and variance-covariance results can inform an argument about internal structure. They cannot alone establish construct validity, explain the cause of an association or distinguish halo from genuine criterion covariance.

The measurement route fits unidimensional ordered-response models. The multivariate G-theory route decomposes variation and covariance in observed scores; it is not a multidimensional latent-variable model. Its current scope is one or two random measurement facets, with supported crossing/nesting and fixed score components. More column names do not extend that scope. Criterion facets, fixed subscore columns and random tasks represent different questions and must not be interchanged just to fit an example. In each application, define the rated unit, target population, score coding and generalization conditions before choosing the analysis.

For readers of Language Testing, the intended value is a reproducible path from an assessment question to interpretable measurement, planning and feedback evidence. The journal’s author guidance welcomes empirical and theoretical language-assessment research and requires a contribution to knowledge. Accordingly, the examples should explain what an analysis changes about score interpretation or assessment design. A list of functions, an attractive plot or a software comparison alone does not establish that contribution. Journal publication is a separate research objective, not a condition for releasing the package.

Application workflows and completion conditions

The following track 0.2.4 workflow requirements. They extend the existing examples and result interfaces; they do not replace unresolved statistical requirements or imply that new estimators have been implemented.

For plan selection, retain source-design and future-plan differences, score units and user-specified decision criteria. A pointwise ribbon is not a simultaneous confidence band; overlap is not a paired test. Screening many plans does not provide selection-adjusted uncertainty or establish an optimal plan. The meaning of relative versus absolute decisions and the practical burden of tasks and raters must accompany any recommendation. There is no universal adequate-reliability cutoff or automatic winner rule.

Remaining visualization refinements

The following track refinements to existing result interfaces before adding another graphics system. Unchecked items remain planned work:

Dense integer-count D-study grids and residual PCA displays already exist; their teaching paths should expose those capabilities. MFRM simulation and G theory answer different score and planning questions, so using both is not mandatory. A general Plotly renderer and arbitrary-facet simulation planner are later extensions, not prerequisites for these refinements. Common-recording school comparisons share the linking assumptions and unverified workflow boundary described below for annual assessments.

Version allocation: 0.2.4 and later

Three descriptions distinguish availability from scientific maturity:

  • Available within the stated scope: implemented for the documented model, design and assumptions. This does not imply suitability for every dataset.
  • Incomplete / experimental: a result can be calculated, but a named aspect of its statistical performance or interpretation remains unestablished.
  • Unavailable: the operation is not implemented or is not supported for the selected model or data. An experimental label does not supply a missing method.

An experimental method may pass numerical checks. Conversely, a supported method may fail on particular data. Keep numerical status, uncertainty type and interpretation notes with saved results and exported tables.

The unresolved issue depends on the procedure. Two-family GPCM retains incomplete general identification and boundary qualification; available local intervals do not settle those questions. An integration failure may be repaired by explicit higher-order refitting. A slope approaching zero while its location and steps diverge is a different problem: response probabilities can remain finite, and more integration points do not supply valid intervals for those original coordinates. The component-interval help explains this distinction; boundary-aware estimation and inference remain separate development work. Corrected GPCM JML estimates an adjusted-equation root, and its root covariance does not establish centering at the structural truth. Common-plan refit/delta intervals have demonstrated small-sample undercoverage and remain ineligible for inferential use. Population intervals, slope profiles, REML target profiles and the extended G-score method retain their stated asymptotic or experimental calibration. Increasing simulation repetitions alone cannot resolve a wrong target, remaining bias or an unsuitable reference distribution.

Conservative regions have a different basis. The mean-square region has a joint coverage lower bound for its declared fixed-score future plans under independent normal ANOVA strata; the signed covariance regression region has its own pointwise conservative argument. Their numerical checks do not prove all floating-point errors harmless, and their bounds can be uninformatively wide. Approximate F has no corresponding exact pivot and has documented undercoverage in small sources. The Validation column distinguishes the approximation from the experimental numerical projection of a conservative region. Conditional Person posterior intervals instead condition on their calibration/prior; they do not become calibration-inclusive confidence intervals by passing integration checks.

Purpose Included in 0.2.4 within its documented scope Incomplete or experimental Planned after 0.2.4
Measurement RSM/PCM MML and JML; RSM/PCM CML structural estimates and identified interaction contrasts with conditional-information intervals; one-slope-family GPCM; supported diagnostics, category outputs, reliability/strata, scoring and calibration reuse. Two-family GMFRM estimation, conditional scoring and available intervals; corrected GPCM JML point/scoring results; Jeffreys-penalized RSM/PCM point estimation; population intervals whose performance is not fully established. MML fixed Person anchors, initially RSM/PCM; broader GMFRM/population uncertainty evaluation; scoped native Bayesian estimation and multidimensional rubric models; later population, timing and attribute extensions as described in the post-release priorities.
G-theory planning Supported crossed/nested G/D studies, identifiable incomplete-source estimation, composites/differences, complete future plans, plots including signed error-source contributions by plan, balanced ANOVA component SEs/intervals and SEM intervals, one-facet G/Phi intervals, approximate MLS individual-plan G/Phi intervals for balanced two-crossed-facet sources, and scoped paired plan-difference intervals. Explicit delta coefficient SEs/normal-reference intervals; experimental approximate-F and mean-square-region coefficient intervals; target-REML variance/covariance component, G/Phi and SEM intervals for balanced/identifiable incomplete sources; signed balanced-source covariance intervals. Plots retain original points, numerical failures and method-specific qualifications. General small-sample calibration remains incomplete. General bootstrap alternatives, robust/simultaneous inference and sparse or unequal future rating plans.
Feedback and decisions Supported individual reports, agreement/reference comparisons, criterion accuracy, centrality, DFF sensitivity checks, exploratory all-pair bias summaries and plots with explicit availability, conditional cut probabilities and fixed-plan classification/SEM. GMFRM feedback and descriptive diagnostics; common-plan refit/delta intervals, including their Jeffreys routes, remain numerically available but inferentially unqualified. General screening accuracy and performance under estimated or shifted ability distributions are not established. Conditional bias screens do not supply collection-wide multiplicity control. Qualified calibration-inclusive decisions, broader diagnostic evaluation, additional-rating allocation and rank/winner uncertainty.

Standalone FACETS-result visualization uses read_facets_results() and plot() for reported element measures and fit statistics. Source IDs, labels, precision, status and unavailable rows remain available for inspection and export. Shared-axis Wright maps require compatible source coordinates to be declared. This descriptive import does not provide external frozen-calibration scoring, joint uncertainty or a validation of the source analysis. Optional Graphfile imports redraw reported category-probability and expected-score coordinates, preserving scale/category identity, precision and unavailable points. They do not align curves with element measures or reconstruct an external calibration. Broader external-calibration reuse remains a later extension.

Anchors, linking/imports, feature analysis, assigned-score imputation and eligible pooling, and separate random-rater/testlet models remain included within their documented restrictions. Stan/brms code export supports its implemented combinations: RSM/PCM and one-family GPCM in both formats, and two-family GPCM in Stan. Supported fixed facet/group and retained step constraints are preserved. Code export is not a native Bayesian estimator or a guarantee about prior choice or credible intervals.

Location anchors use internal coordinates; ordinary fit uncertainty conditions on their supplied values. The bounded source-covariance interval extension above is opt-in. Person direct/group anchors require JML; MML rejects them. New ordinary fits center each declared facet across all levels, including anchors and group totals. Use centering_scope = "remainder" to reproduce the earlier convention. For ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML, centering_scope = "anchor_origin" instead lets direct or group anchors replace their facet’s centering, as FACETS does. This needs an unanchored, active noncenter facet. Group targets are repeated means, not native per-element contributions. The ordinary constrained likelihood is retained: native multi-group numerical results and general extreme handling are not reproduced automatically. Thresholds and slopes are not carried by the location-anchor table. See the linking tutorial for a complete example and the distinction from fixed-calibration scoring.

Anchor alignment and its qualification

Ordinary fitting and anchor review now accept centering_scope = "facet" (default), "remainder" (legacy reproduction), and "anchor_origin" (direct or group anchors replace centering in ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML). The default convention centers the whole declared facet, including fixed values. An anchor does not implicitly select the population mean, variance, threshold structure or uncentered facet. These choices must match before results can be compared with TAM or ConQuest. Ordinary fitting, saved refit settings and the scoped population-model correspondence and the migration workflow are checked; release integration remains incomplete. The fixed-SD, intercept-only RSM/PCM anchor-origin route has conditional facet/population intervals and optional independent-source covariance propagation. Broader anchored population specifications remain outside that interval extension. One-family GPCM slope and curve intervals have a separate supported scope, described below.

Completion requires more than matching a few estimates:

Existing results will not be converted merely by changing their labels or reloading a file. A fit under a different constraint system generally needs re-estimation. Anchor alignment alone does not add uncertainty from estimating anchors; the bounded source-covariance extension requires explicit arguments. Neither promises equivalent defaults across programs. make_anchor_table() preserves fitted numeric values by default. Rounding individual anchors can break their joint zero sum; use digits explicitly for a display copy and review any rounded values before recalibration.

Conditional intervals for supported ordinary RSM/PCM MML facet estimates already exist; verifying them under the revised constraints is part of this release work. This differs from propagating uncertainty in externally estimated anchors. Bias-screening SEs and conditional bounds retain their screening interpretation. For one fitted two-facet interaction in fixed-N(0,1), fixed-grid direct RSM/PCM MML, mfrm_facet_intervals(interaction = ...) now provides joint-information cell and contrast intervals. This separate extension uses all nuisance-parameter uncertainty; it is not automatic anchor alignment, a replacement for screening, or a guarantee of simultaneous inference. Anchors, GPCM, population regression and multiple interaction terms remain outside this joint-cell interval route.

Across-year assessments with common recordings

An annual speech contest can have different contestants but use the same recorded speeches for rater calibration. The recorded performance, rather than the identity of a returning judge, can connect years. The intended outcomes are changes in each judge’s severity, a panel-wide shift in scoring, and differences between annual contestant groups on a defensible common scale. This is not a study of individual contestant growth.

Two approaches need different qualifications: jointly estimate years with a shared unknown measure for each common recording, or fix previously estimated recording measures in later calibrations. Shared performances do not require known anchor values. Fixing estimated values excludes their source uncertainty unless that uncertainty is separately propagated. A common three-minute task format or unchanged criterion names alone does not establish scale invariance.

Existing functions provide parts of this analysis, but a complete common-recording workflow and its year-difference intervals are not yet verified. Person anchors require JML; current MML rejects them. detect_anchor_drift() removes a common-element offset: using the judges themselves as the linking set can remove a panel-wide severity change. Its SE ratios are descriptive screens, not formal tests of longitudinal change. anchor_to_baseline() checks that fixed values were retained; that check does not establish their stability.

The linking guide and speech-contest design example explain these choices and current limits in the development documentation. A new longitudinal estimator or formal uncertainty procedure is not a release prerequisite. The later workflow must preserve individual ratings before consensus, distinguish training from operational ratings, and review video-versus-live scoring and the stability of criteria and categories. It must allow annual severity to change without imposing the same panel mean separately in every year.

Comparison-specific identification review

Native RSM/PCM CML now supplies full-rank structural estimates and conditional information intervals through fit_mfrm(method = "CML") and mfrm_facet_intervals(). It conditions on Person totals and requires no ability population distribution. This addresses fixed-exposure incidental-parameter bias under the documented conditional-model and information-growth assumptions; a more accurate JML covariance would not do so. Increasing Person count alone does not supply information in every identified structural direction. The model must remain valid for the actual rating assignment and missingness process. Its separate result class has no ability estimates or population SD. The existing population-SD-standardized contrasts use the full joint MML delta method, including uncertainty in the fitted SD. Matching full RSM/PCM MML interaction fits now support this transformation via comparison_review in mfrm_facet_intervals(), under an explicitly declared common intercept-only normal population; native intervals also support origin-specific means. Regular standardized inference requires an identifiable, correctly specified marginal model and a true population SD strictly above zero. Finite-quadrature agreement diagnoses numerical sensitivity; it does not establish these assumptions or guarantee continuous-model inference as sample size grows. General GPCM inference follows MML; JML remains useful for descriptive estimates and FACETS comparisons. Explicit comparison-only CML also supplies intervals for identified interaction contrasts in deficient models. Neither route guarantees arbitrary finite-sample coverage or completes the broader school/annual calibration workflow.

The common-recording workflow must distinguish a shared measurement scale from an identifiable differential-facet comparison. For example, a judge who only rates School A may contribute to a linked calibration while their School A-versus-B effect remains unobserved. Shared recordings supply that particular comparison only when their group identities and rating contexts support it, or when additional assumptions are explicitly imposed.

The comparison contract distinguishes a rater’s school difference relative to a declared panel, the difference between two raters’ school differences, and a separately modeled population contrast. The panel and its weights must remain explicit. PCM response comparisons also depend on the step owner. Bounded RSM/PCM checks support this distinction, including partial identification and comparisons that remain unidentified after adding neutral common recordings. describe_mfrm_data(comparisons = ...) now exposes a bounded prospective RSM/PCM interaction review with explicit contrast weights. It distinguishes full, partial and target nonidentification under the conditional response model; positive MML conditional ranks remain separate from marginal identification. IdentificationBasis distinguishes unrestricted-Person response-model identification, conditional identification relying on population restrictions, and CML conditional support. The accompanying explanation separates common population assumptions from scale coding; a free-Person map does not make MML inference distribution-free. Unsupported external-reference and broader invariance workflows remain outside this scoped review. Its results can accompany DFF summaries, plots and reports after response/origin alignment checks. They do not classify the residual/refit effects themselves. For matching joint fits, interaction_effect_table(fit, comparison_review = ...) and summary(fit, comparison_review = ...) return descriptive interaction contrasts after full conditional-rank and numerical checks. The executed teaching example allows group-specific population means; MML’s positive conditional rank remains distinct from global marginal identification. Explicit fit_mfrm(fit_scope = "comparisons", comparison_review = ...) now provides a separate descriptive result for invariant targets in rank-deficient RSM/PCM models. It preserves the observed likelihood and retains unavailable targets, with recession/numerical checks and the same MML identification limits. With a CML review, it instead uses conditional support at observed Person totals, optimizes only identified directions and supplies conditional-information SEs, pointwise 95% Wald intervals and joint covariance for identified targets. Unidentified targets remain missing. Broader school-calibration qualification and finite-sample interval performance remain separate work. Saved CML comparison fits now use mfrm_facet_intervals(fit) for a selected confidence level, existing interval plots and APA tables. Missing estimates retain labeled rows without points; the same fit and review remain in the saved result. This display route does not add Person scoring or ordinary fit diagnostics to comparison-only objects.

Bounded GPCM checks distinguish location, component-slope, effective-product and response-curve comparisons. Unequal slopes can reverse a response contrast across ability even when the parameters are locally identified. The reviewed one-family JML/MML and two-family MML maps have explicitly limited local numerical evidence; disconnected-product counterexamples retain the existing fit rejection. Predicting an unobserved crossing requires the product-model assumption. These checks do not add school interactions to GPCM, establish global identification, or provide automatic GPCM comparison reporting.

The remaining items are prerequisites for the later verified common-recording/DFF workflow. The prospective review, descriptive JML/MML estimates and asymptotic CML intervals remain distinct. They do not establish global marginal identification or calibrated DFF classification, and no new 0.2.4 release gate is added. The remaining work does not authorize arbitrary constraints to make a deficient model fit.

Planned MML Person anchors

Fixed Person anchors are a requested extension after 0.2.4, initially for RSM/PCM. They remain unavailable in MML until the following conditions are met; shared unknown recordings in a joint fit are a different design.

Differential facet functioning: displays and remaining inference

The displays are existing 0.2.4 capabilities. Formal DFF uncertainty and MML Person anchors are later work, not newly completed estimators or new release requirements. See the DFF plot help and the linking guide above for the current interpretation boundaries.

Model scope

RSM uses shared category steps. PCM uses steps belonging to the declared step_facet; GPCM additionally declares the facet whose levels have slopes. These roles may differ where supported. The two-family product-slope model has its own restrictions, including second-owner steps. Multiple independent threshold owners and arbitrary combinations of model extensions are not implied by accepting arbitrary column names.

Saved one-family GPCM Person scores from predict_mfrm_units() can now be attached to mfrm_results(..., scores = ...) for reports, export and saved replay. EAP, posterior SD and continuous conditional posterior intervals retain the actual scoring priors and numerical review states. They exclude calibration and population estimation uncertainty and do not replace diagnostic normal bands.

Explicit rating contexts in category_curves_report(fit, newdata = contexts) now support native one- and two-family GPCM MML curves and cumulative 50% thresholds, with source readiness and unavailable intervals retained. This extends descriptive calculation; two-family inference remains provisional.

Read the GPCM guide and interval guide before selecting an uncertainty method. Current distinctions include:

  • Ordinary JML location SEs are exploratory. Corrected-JML local root SEs do not supply formal confidence intervals for structural parameters.
  • Computed GMFRM bounds do not establish their repeated-sample coverage. Partial or unavailable results retain their reasons.
  • Two-family step/curve intervals, ordinary fit/bias tests and Wright/Pathway maps are unavailable. Other supported outputs have their own interpretation.
  • Conditional Person scoring holds calibration fixed and excludes uncertainty from estimating those calibration parameters. A prior appropriate for one cohort may be inappropriate for another.
  • High rater separation reliability indicates distinguishable severity differences; it is not evidence that raters agree.

Incomplete assignments, extreme scores, missing categories and weak links can affect estimation and precision differently. A connected rating graph alone does not establish identification. No single sample-size threshold establishes that all supported methods will work well.

Generalizability theory

mfrm_g_study() and mfrm_d_study() support one or two named random facets, crossed or with one nested within the other while Persons are crossed. Score components are fixed. ANOVA handles complete balanced data; MINQUE(0) handles identifiable incomplete or unequal sources.

D-studies project complete balanced future plans, including weighted composites and signed score differences. They do not estimate the reliability of an arbitrary sparse future roster. Negative or indefinite component estimates remain visible; availability is assessed separately for each metric.

mfrm_multivariate_d_compare() provides approximate paired-delta intervals for prespecified plan differences with two crossed facets under an explicit normal-random-effects assumption. These intervals do not supply component confidence intervals or uncertainty bands around each D-study curve. Measurement SEM and sampling uncertainty in an estimated variance component are different quantities.

For balanced ANOVA, confint() now provides component sampling SEs and pointwise Ting MLS intervals for one score or a fixed composite, under an explicit normal-random-effects assumption. One or two crossed random facets and the supported balanced nested design are included. Negative estimates and unrestricted endpoints are retained alongside the interval’s intersection with nonnegative variances. For two original scores, explicit gci and regression_region methods now supply signed covariance-component intervals. The generalized method has approximate coverage and separate endpoint Monte Carlo diagnostics; the conservative enclosure can be extremely wide with few facet levels. SE and interval availability are reported separately. Scalar component intervals also have an explicit experimental reml_profile option for identifiable incomplete sources. Original MINQUE points remain unchanged; separate REML centers and numerical diagnostics accompany squared-unit bounds. This inversion does not calculate a sampling SE or qualify nominal coverage. Two-score covariance also has an explicit experimental joint reml_profile option for identifiable incomplete sources, preserving signed endpoints and separate REML centers. Its chi-square calibration can under-cover with few facet levels; incomplete-source coverage is not established. It does not replace the balanced methods or become an automatic default.

For one-facet G, explicit spectral_f intervals additionally accept retained incomplete or unequal source ratings. They project out facet effects and invert an exact F pivot under independent normal Person effects and residuals, with positive residual variance and residual degrees of freedom. Paired plan differences map the same confidence set. Original MINQUE points and unavailable states remain visible. Removing facet directions can lose information; exact coverage does not imply narrow intervals or robustness to selective missingness. This is not a Phi, SEM, nested or multifacet method, and is not an automatic default.

G/Phi additionally have explicit method = "delta" sampling SEs and normal-reference intervals for the original ANOVA/MINQUE estimator, including supported nested and incomplete sources. This is a first-order approximation, with documented undercoverage and unavailable estimates in some small or incomplete sources. The full component sampling covariance is propagated; coefficient SE is distinct from measurement SEM. Tables, forests and ribbons retain wide bounds outside [0,1] and their qualifications. It does not replace existing defaults or supply SEM or paired-difference intervals.

G/Phi and measurement SEM have an explicit experimental reml_profile option for identifiable incomplete or unequal sources as well as balanced sources. It fits the used ratings under normal effects and preserves the original ANOVA/MINQUE points, reporting the separate REML estimates and numerical diagnostics. Its chi-square calibration is approximate; finite-sample and boundary checks do not yet justify an automatic default. Broader incomplete-source plan-difference inference remains separate. SEM limits come from a direct error-variance profile and a square-root transformation. They describe an interval around the REML center, without enumerating remote disconnected accepted regions. Limited boundary checks showed below-nominal inclusion; providing this explicit approximation does not qualify a default. plot(g, intervals = TRUE, assumption = "normal") shows the existing component intervals for one score, multiple score panels or a fixed composite, retaining negative estimates and unavailable reasons in base and ggplot outputs. For individual D-study plans from a balanced one-facet source, confint() now supplies exact F intervals for G under independent normal random effects. The source degrees of freedom are retained when transforming to different future counts. Phi now uses a generalized confidence interval with separate Monte Carlo endpoint diagnostics; it does not guarantee exact frequentist coverage. For balanced two-crossed- random-facet sources, individual-plan G/Phi intervals now default to approximate MLS null inversion. Undefined widths are conservatively retained and flagged separately from numerical availability. Normal-model checks support this choice within the evaluated designs; it does not guarantee uniform coverage or narrow intervals in small sources. Alternative explicit experimental choices remain: "approximate_f", "mean_square_region" and "reml_profile". None is selected automatically. The mean-square region requires lpSolve and can be very conservative. The first two require a complete balanced crossed ANOVA source and independent normal effects. REML profiles use the normal likelihood of the used ratings and also accept identifiable incomplete or unequal sources; they require lme4 and minqa. A forest plot() compares methods within future plans on one shared axis, with a common legend and retained unavailable results. Separate panels remain optional. For ordinary planning, plot(d, metric = "Phi", intervals = TRUE, assumption = "normal") calculates and overlays coefficient intervals on the existing D-study curves. One method is shown at a time; selected scores or composites are handled together. Saved intervals can optionally be reused, using a list when several scores/composites are selected. Ribbons retain gaps, method limitations and numerical diagnostics. Their appearance does not establish simultaneous coverage across scores or metrics. Small normal-model evaluations of the approximate F method found coverage, width and availability limitations, including at zero components and changed future counts. Delta-method SE results do not alone validate coefficient intervals. A preliminary comparison of joint-parameter Monte Carlo and a basic parametric bootstrap found different limitations: Monte Carlo intervals can be very wide, while the evaluated bootstrap rule can withhold intervals at inadmissible point estimates and miss true values even among returned intervals. These findings concern the specific procedures evaluated, not all Monte Carlo or bootstrap methods. Neither alternative is currently a public method or a qualified default. A missing point estimate does not by itself make a confidence interval unavailable; the existing methods keep these statuses separate. A joint-deviance confidence-region candidate also showed width limitations in a bounded feasibility assessment: mathematically justified joint coverage does not by itself ensure useful coefficient precision. It remains a research construction. Further method selection distinguishes G from Phi and retains boundary and nuisance-parameter uncertainty. The MLS route adds a checked approximation for balanced individual plans; incomplete-source calibration remains separate. Wide intervals remain visible even when they provide limited help in choosing a plan. There is no universal acceptable coefficient interval width. Specify the intended decision and acceptable precision before comparing methods; a narrow interval is not evidence of accurate coverage. Providing useful calculations does not require narrow intervals for every small or sparse source. See the coefficient-interval help and the G-theory tutorial for reasons, results and references. These limits do not imply that all two-facet interval methods are invalid. Expanded paired-plan intervals also remain under review. For one-facet G differences, confint() with a reference plan now maps the entire F confidence set, including interior extrema. This supplies model-based coverage of at least the requested level, without extending the two-facet delta approximation to other designs. One-facet Phi differences now map the entire generalized interval, retaining approximate frequentist coverage and joint Monte Carlo endpoint bands. Both retain the dependence between plans; subtracting marginal limits is not the calculation.

SEM sampling intervals are now available from balanced one/two-facet crossed and supported nested sources. confint(d, parm = "RelativeSEM" or "AbsoluteSEM", assumption = "normal") combines the source mean squares, uses chi-square or MLS error-variance limits, and takes square roots. The single-term chi-square case is exact under its positive-variance normal model; MLS remains approximate, with undercoverage/conservatism documented. One-facet SEM differences map their common error-SD interval through reference. SEM curve ribbons and saved interval forests use score units.

Balanced nested G/Phi intervals and comparisons now use the one-facet distributional reduction when every future child count per parent equals the source count. Parent counts may vary; both facets remain random. G retains exact normal-model inference and Phi retains approximate GCI coverage. Nested SEM differences need a common future child count across plans, which may differ from the source count. They preserve the chi-square/MLS qualification of the base interval. General balanced nested G/Phi intervals now accept explicit experimental approximate-F and mean-square-region methods. The F derivation uses expected mean squares, with discrepancies in printed nested Phi formulas explained in help. Limited checks identify severe boundary availability losses for approximate F and wide region intervals. General crossed/nested two-facet G/Phi/SEM comparisons accept method = "mean_square_region" with reference: the difference is enclosed using projections of the same simultaneous source region. Coverage is conservative under the stated normal model; the enclosure need not be the tight image and can be very wide. The region method also supports individual SEM intervals. These explicit choices do not qualify an automatic default.

Plots include source-component panels, covariance heatmaps, D-study curves and facet-count panels, with colour and monochrome options. See the G-theory tutorial. These observed-score analyses do not estimate latent MFRM reliability or pass/fail classification accuracy.

G/D-study and paired-comparison objects now enter mfrm_report() and the shared table/CSV/HTML export workflow directly. Supplied saved intervals retain source checks, method qualifications and unavailable rows. The editable templates/gtheory-report.Rmd joins source design, score weights, components, G/Phi, error variances, SEM, plan contrasts and figures with manuscript prompts.

Rater feedback across application areas

Rater networks now include signed pairwise alpha, magnitude-weighted network severity/SWS/PUS, person-cluster halo contrast intervals and an optional binary ERGM adapter using statnet. All connect to reports and full-table export. These are complementary observed-score/network analyses: SWS/PUS have no calibrated universal cutoffs, bootstrap intervals condition on the observed rater set and withhold undefined resamples, and ERGM requires a declared tie threshold, missing-dyad assumption and backend convergence/GOF review. Valued ERGMs, estimated-edge uncertainty and general rater-population halo inference remain outside this adapter’s scope. See the network guide for examples.

mfrm_residual_network() connects fitted standardized residuals to signed correlation networks, optional common-person hierarchical groups, three plot views and the shared report API. Groups remain exploratory; EGA, jointly fitted residual networks, automatic dimensionality decisions and group-stability inference are not implemented by this route. The help explains validation and the separate supervised role of random forests in rater-type research.

The supported reports distinguish severity, fit, category use, agreement, residual dependence and accuracy against a supplied criterion. A screening flag requires substantive review; it does not demonstrate rater incompetence or justify automatic exclusion. Individual interval overlap is not a test of the difference between two raters.

Centrality is currently described by RSM residual/fit indices and the spread of rater-owned PCM thresholds. Halo networks describe observed-score associations; they do not separate genuine criterion relationships from an impression spreading across criteria. A horn effect is an unfavorable impression spilling over into other ratings, not a negative correlation or high severity alone. No dedicated horn classification is available. Direct severity/centrality (FM-SC) and halo mixture (MRFM-H) models are not implemented in 0.2.4. See the methods guide for the distinction between these targets and local dependence.

Conditional probabilities of being above a cut, fixed-plan classification accuracy/consistency, and future performance are separate targets. Report which decision rule and population were used, and whether calibration was held fixed. The reporting tutorial explains denominators, uncertainty and the scope of available reports.

Pillar milestones and progress

The three purposes share one release sequence. The table below preserves the accepted capability and workflow outcomes; it does not turn counts of completed items into a percentage of statistical validity, effort or release readiness.

Purpose Accepted baseline within the declared scope Remaining finalization
Measurement Model and derived-output checks, anchor migration, native RSM/PCM CML and identified comparisons, MML population-SD contrasts, estimator-specific guides and saved reuse. Preserve admitted mathematical/statistical claims and experimental boundaries through the latest report connections, then qualify the matching source and environments.
G-theory planning Scoped component, individual-plan and paired-plan uncertainty; integrated summaries, figures, editable reports and saved workflows. Preserve source/future design, score units, fixed weights and method-specific uncertainty. Arbitrary future rosters and allocation optimization remain later work.
Feedback and decisions Supported diagnostics, report modules, fixed-calibration decision summaries, interpretation guidance and saved workflows. Complete the selected workflow checks while retaining source context, unavailable evidence and conditional uncertainty. General calibration-inclusive decisions and direct rater-effect models remain later work.

The 0.2.4 diagnostic allocation retains the recorded estimator-specific fit statistics. In particular, EAP plug-in MnSq remains descriptive, without an expectation-one guarantee. A new posterior-averaged parameter-fit statistic requires a separate definition and validation and is allocated to later work. It is not a prerequisite for publishing the existing descriptive diagnostics.

Practical two-family use now has a paired-study guide covering numerical delivery, interval coverage, observed runtime, rater overlap, sample-size interpretation and unavailable bias/anchor operations. fit_mfrm(progress = TRUE) provides phase and elapsed-time feedback; iteration limits do not predict time remaining. Exact probability reuse reduces duplicated EM work without changing the target or admission criteria. The latest successful two-family automatic fit also shares its complete numerical qualification with subsequent intervals in the same R session, conditional on exact fit, memory-setting and numerical- backend identity. This transient reuse is absent from saved fits; fresh sessions recalculate. Further numerical work should address information-check cost within each fit and unresolved curvature/integration failures. New two-family adaptive fits cap the total-gradient review at the interval procedure’s per-Person scale, activating the existing bounded finish when necessary. Older saved fits retain their recorded rule, and independent interval checks remain mandatory. Stronger delivery or inferential claims require matched validation; the existing experimental allocation and source-specific evidence remain explicit.

The application workflows remain accepted within their scope. The common-recording annual workflow, calibration-inclusive decisions and direct centrality/halo models remain later work. Documenting an unavailable output does not implement it. Executed examples and editorial review do not establish measured novice comprehension.

Completion milestones for 0.2.4

Each milestone closes an outcome, with evidence for the declared scope. The first two can proceed together; workflow corrections follow any changes to the API or inferential specification. Their acceptance precedes substantive freeze, which precedes final delivery qualification and publication.

Milestone Completion condition Current state
Final API, mathematical and inferential specification Each supported target and procedure has explicit model assumptions, identification/existence conditions, an applicable derivation, independent implementation checks, numerical eligibility and evidence adequate for its statistical claims. Inputs, defaults, uncertainty and unavailable operations agree. Resolve required gaps; justify experimental and later allocations. Accepted for the current release allocation. Capability guidance, help and user outputs agree with the accepted method-family evidence, including uncertainty and refusal labels. Fixed-default/opt-in-auto MML, descriptive diagnostics and experimental/later allocations are explicit. Native comparison follow-up and general coverage research remain unfinished. Exact, asymptotic, approximate and descriptive claims retain their distinct scope.
Complete supported user workflows The declared entry points lead to interpretable results, supported plots/tables, export and fresh-session reuse. Errors and unavailable results preserve their meaning; help and examples agree with the accepted mathematical specification. Accepted for the current release allocation, combining scoped teaching, reporting, plotting and saved-result evidence with affected-route corrections and fresh-session review. Saved intervals preserve targets, uncertainty, experimental qualifications and unavailable states. This is not a fresh complete run of every example or measured novice comprehension.
Substantive specification and source freeze The preceding outcomes are accepted; functionality, inference, numerical procedures and migration behavior are settled. One identified source and candidate archive agree with metadata, help, examples and release notes. A matching local candidate now includes G/D, network and anchor/bias/model-choice reports, study declarations and the bounded display/input corrections. Its source and distribution correspondence is verified. This local selection is separate from main-source integration, final environment qualification and publication.
Final package and environment qualification The selected source has attributable package, supported-platform, dependency, saved-result and documentation checks. Remaining failures and execution-time requirements are resolved; the package and website represent the same accepted behavior. Open, with the missing distributed regression completed and its affected repairs checked in an installed package. Current tutorials, targeted help/site generation and saved reports are verified. Earlier examples/manual checks retain their original source scope; combined evidence is not a fresh clean complete check of the successor. Remaining supported-platform, external-link, website and source-integration qualification stay explicit.
Verified publication Authorized source, package and documentation are published consistently, with installed/downloaded outputs checked. GitHub availability, CRAN submission and CRAN acceptance have separate recorded states. Not published; submission is not acceptance.

RSM/PCM CML supplies conditional structural inference without a fitted ability distribution; it supplies neither Person abilities nor a population SD. MML supplies the supported population-model and general GPCM inference routes. Population-SD-standardized contrasts use the same fit’s SD and applicable joint delta covariance. JML remains a point-estimation/FACETS-comparison route for structural parameters; its numerical or root uncertainty is not automatically a structural-truth confidence interval. Existing conditional scoring and descriptive diagnostics retain their own documented scope. These roles do not by themselves change the default estimator or make every downstream operation available for every result class.

RSM-versus-PCM likelihood-ratio tests require the PCM to retain every fixed interaction term in the RSM. More free category steps alone do not make a PCM an extension of an RSM with omitted interactions. The nesting review now withholds those tests while retaining otherwise eligible information-criterion comparisons. Recreate affected saved comparisons from their fitted objects; this correction does not require refitting the models.

Use accepted source- and scope-matched evidence to close these milestones. Mathematical acceptance distinguishes four questions: whether a result follows under the stated model and regularity conditions; whether the implementation matches that result; whether the numerical solution is admissible; and whether the evidence supports the claimed statistical performance. An asymptotic result is not a universal finite-sample guarantee, and numerical agreement alone does not establish coverage. Evaluate existing evidence against the actual claim before deciding whether a derivation, correction or further study is needed. Additional tests or numerical studies must address a changed behavior, missing required evidence or unresolved finding; an untried condition alone does not require another study. A warning cannot substitute for repairing an incorrect supported calculation. If delivery repairs change an inferential procedure, return to the affected substantive milestone and qualify the change before selecting the replacement source. Unaffected evidence remains valid.

Release completion checklist

Checked items are accepted within their stated scope and support the milestones above; the detailed items are not additional milestones. Existing G-theory derivations and design-specific checks retain their scope, as do the API repairs and reviewed workflows. The selected specification and implemented workflows are accepted with their stated qualifications. Candidate archives retain their source-specific evidence; the latest workflow changes still require a matching source selection. Package/platform qualification and publication remain open. Research tasks below do not delay release merely because they remain unfinished; incorrect calculations, misleading claims or broken supported workflows do require correction.

Post-release priorities

These items remain unfinished. Listing them does not promise a particular release date or assign them all to 0.2.5.

Direction and staged delivery

The main purpose remains measurement involving ratings, assessment planning and useful feedback. Extensions should answer concrete questions about a rating process and its consequences: what a Person’s profile means, which rater or criterion findings need review, and whether another task, another rater or additional scoring time would improve the intended decision.

Existing software already provides multidimensional IRT, Bayesian estimation, response-time models and cognitive diagnosis. The development objective is to make selected rating workflows usable together, preserving their different estimands, assumptions and uncertainty. This is not a claim that these model families originate in mfrmr. Named methodological starting points include Bayesian GMFRM, multidimensional GMFRM, rater-effects cognitive diagnosis and joint ratings/rating-time models. Their response equations and inference targets require explicit mapping before adoption. Matching a model name is not sufficient.

Stage and tentative version range Intended deliverable Boundary for the first release of that capability
Interoperability: first 0.2.5 candidates Reusable model specifications and a checked path from joint external draws to new contrasts and posterior targets. Clarify supported TAM imports and ConQuest comparisons. Extend the existing read-only saved-summary return for exported RSM/PCM/GPCM. An imported marginal summary is not a native calibration or joint uncertainty estimate.
Bayesian workflows: subsequent 0.2.5 candidates Optional fitting and scoring through CmdStan/cmdstanr, with explicit priors and joint calibration uncertainty. Build on the same export/result path. Add new-Person scoring, external calibration uncertainty and broader slope families as separately qualified increments; preserve current MML defaults.
Rubric profiles: 0.3.x candidates Prespecified multidimensional MFRM/GMFRM, joint Person-profile uncertainty and criterion/rater feedback. Start with low-dimensional simple structure and unit slopes, then admit free-slope variants. Identification, numerical accuracy and usefulness of subscores need separate evidence.
Rating processes: later 0.3.x / 0.4.x candidates Direct centrality, restricted rater classes, and response-time/rating-time extensions chosen for specific assessment questions. Qualify the branches separately. A combined model with every effect is not the initial goal.
Diagnostic attributes: 0.4.x and later candidates Explicit skill-Q specifications and a bounded rater-effects CDM workflow for mastery/profile feedback. Begin with a small specified skill structure and a matched established reference. Broader response scales and automatic Q/class selection are separate extensions.
Planning and decisions throughout Broader future rating rosters, uncertainty in plan comparisons and, eventually, additional-rating allocation under cost constraints. Specify the score, generalization population and decision loss. Keep classical G-theory and model-based predictive planning distinguishable.

These ranges express a dependency order, not a release calendar. A useful branch can be delivered without waiting for every other model in its stage. Each delivery includes its supported scoring/reporting path and saved reuse, with unavailable results retained. A converged fit alone does not complete a feedback or assessment-planning workflow.

ConQuest, TAM and Stan: use, compare and extend

The immediate benefit is to let an analyst reuse a supported external result, inspect an exported model, or compare a matched calculation without losing the meaning of its scores and uncertainty. These are different operations.

Connection Already available in 0.2.4 Next useful increment
TAM import_tam_fit() imports supported unidimensional MML results for summaries and point-only Wright maps. Multifacet conditions become DesignCell locations; separate facet effects and their joint covariance are not reconstructed. Extend source-aware reporting first; recover separate facets or transformed uncertainty only with an identified parameter map and the required joint covariance.
ConQuest build_conquest_overlap_bundle() and review_conquest_overlap() support a narrow binary, single-facet latent-regression comparison. Broader research comparisons do not expand this public API. Add matched polytomous additive RSM/PCM cases before more general GPCM exchange. Reuse conquestr where suitable for execution and reading, retaining original outputs and settings.
Stan/brms export_mfrm_model() writes model bundles. RSM/PCM and one-family GPCM support both formats, including supported fixed facet/group anchors; two-family GPCM supports Stan. read_mfrm_posterior() connects saved summaries to figures, credible intervals and shared reports. Preserve estimated-population GPCM specifications, then extend joint-draw contrasts, new credible levels and prediction. Support data/specification input without a preliminary MML fit.

ConQuest already includes multidimensional, multifaceted and Bayesian estimation. TAM supports multidimensional models and faceted slope designs through selected interfaces; the limits of tam.mml.mfr() do not describe all of TAM. The aim is a well-supported rating workflow, with established engines as references and optional connections. A larger model catalogue alone does not establish methodological novelty or practical superiority.

Stan export currently requires a supported native MML fit, unit weights, no interactions/shrinkage and a fixed standard-normal Person population. Fixed anchors are exact constraints; uncertainty from an earlier calibration is not propagated. Person anchors and native two-family anchored fitting remain outside the source-model scope. It preserves the response likelihood and adds explicit structural priors; its posterior is not the original MML estimate or confidence interval. The read-only mfrm_posterior_summary connects saved marginal summaries to summary(), plot(), confint(), long plot tables and mfrm_report(). It checks the matching model-data identity and retains sampling review; confint() retrieves the stored 95% credible interval. It does not provide native MML diagnostics, joint draws, new interval levels or scoring.

Further Bayesian result work should preserve joint draws and chain/iteration identity for new posterior targets while extending the existing report route. Priors, mappings and numerical diagnostics must remain explicit during reuse. Classical G/D coefficients and model-based predictive planning keep separate targets; shared data or reports do not make them interchangeable.

Later comparison and prediction must declare what is new: a rating from an existing Person, a new Person, or a new rater. Existing row-level log_lik conditions on sampled Person abilities and is not a ready-made new-Person validation score. The loo cross-validation guidance explains why the held-out unit and latent-effect treatment must match the task. These extensions are post-0.2.4 work, not additional release blockers.

Model extensions and their acceptance conditions

Computational choices must preserve the requested estimand and precision. Tensor quadrature grows exponentially with the number of continuous dimensions; enumerating unrestricted binary attributes also grows exponentially. Future multidimensional controls therefore need explicit total computational budgets and accuracy diagnostics. Existing one-dimensional point limits do not imply the same cost or accuracy in multiple dimensions. Bayesian sampling is an additional inference route, not an automatic speed improvement.

Assess additions against simpler models and established software with matching response laws, scales and uncertainty targets. Evaluation should include useful outputs, unavailable results, uncertainty, decision or prediction performance, runtime and memory. Empirical applications and intended-user evaluation are needed for claims about practical benefit. Preserve the following ongoing priorities alongside the new model branches.

Relationship to structural equation modeling

Structural equation modeling provides a related framework for connecting measurement models to covariates, other constructs and longitudinal processes. Selected IRT and categorical factor models coincide under matching response laws, scales and constraints. Ordinary ordinal threshold CFA and PCM/GPCM, however, use different category-probability constructions. A common path diagram or a rescaled loading does not establish model or estimator equivalence.

lavaan offers a useful CFA/SEM reference within its supported response and estimation scope. Mplus explicitly includes PCM/GPCM, multidimensional and cross-classified IRT, mixtures and diagnostic classification. Each proposed overlap needs its specific model/estimator combination checked. SEM-based G-theory and dependability methods also exist; these areas are not exclusive to mfrmr.

The planned connection is a bounded rating workflow: specify the measurement and parameter mapping, relate supported latent profiles to a substantive external variable, and preserve uncertainty in results exchanged with other software. Current MML latent regression is a scoped starting point, not a general structural-model API. Point-score export alone does not propagate measurement or shared calibration uncertainty. Plausible-value analyses need compatible downstream conditioning and uncertainty handling; existing fixed-calibration draws do not automatically meet that requirement.

Prioritize matched reference calculations and selected interoperability examples over a general SEM engine. Preserve observation/cluster identities, constraints, uncertainty targets and unsupported states. Native Bayesian development remains based on CmdStan/cmdstanr. Broader path, growth and mediation analysis can use established software when the measurement and uncertainty connection is justified; neither a path diagram nor model fit alone establishes a causal effect or construct validity.

Continuing application and inference priorities

Compatibility principles

Preserve model, scale, category, anchor and uncertainty meanings across saved results, tables, figures and exports. Breaking changes require migration instructions. In 0.2.4 the former standalone drawing functions become private; use the replacements in the plot migration guide. plot_data() and plot_data_components() remain public for extracting data. Unavailable results and their reasons should remain visible rather than being replaced with plausible-looking numbers.
